---
title: "Bridge and Activation"
format: gfm
execute: 
  eval: false
---

This chapter defines the bridge between the base container and the
project-specific Spack environment.

The container should provide only the minimal tools needed to start
Spack reliably. Project-specific compiler, linker, library, and runtime
paths should be activated explicitly after `/work` is mounted and the
project Spack environment is available.

First, ensure the base container environment is conservative:

```{python}
recipe.environ.extend(
    [
        "PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/bin:${PATH:-}",
        "SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true",
        "SPACK_USER_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/spack-user-config",
        "SPACK_USER_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/spack-user-cache",
        "SPACK_MISC_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/spack-misc-cache",
    ]
)
```

Write the updated Singularity definition:

```{python}
definition = recipe_to_definition(recipe)
SINGULARITY_DEF.write_text(definition)
```

Rebuild the sandbox:

```{python}
Client.build(
    image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
    recipe=str(SINGULARITY_DEF),
    options=["--fakeroot", "--sandbox", "--fix-perms", "--force"],
    sudo=False,
)
```

Now write the canonical project activation script. This belongs to the
project, not the base image, because it assumes the project is mounted at
`/work` and that the project Spack environment lives there.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import textwrap

ENV_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

activate_script = r"""
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Canonical project activation for the container runtime.
#
# This script assumes:
#   - the project is mounted at /work
#   - Spack is available at /opt/spack
#   - the project Spack environment lives in /work
#   - the project Spack view is /work/.spack-env/view

set -euo pipefail

unset R_HOME

export SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true
export SPACK_USER_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/spack-user-config
export SPACK_USER_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/spack-user-cache
export SPACK_MISC_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/spack-misc-cache

. /opt/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh

cd /work
spack env activate -d .

export SPACK_VIEW=/work/.spack-env/view
export PATH="${SPACK_VIEW}/bin:${PATH:-}"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="${SPACK_VIEW}/lib/pkgconfig:${SPACK_VIEW}/lib64/pkgconfig:${SPACK_VIEW}/share/pkgconfig:${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:-}"
export CPATH="${SPACK_VIEW}/include:${CPATH:-}"
export LIBRARY_PATH="${SPACK_VIEW}/lib:${SPACK_VIEW}/lib64:${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${SPACK_VIEW}/lib:${SPACK_VIEW}/lib64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"

if command -v R >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export R_HOME="$(R RHOME 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
"""

ACTIVATE_SCRIPT.write_text(textwrap.dedent(activate_script).lstrip())
ACTIVATE_SCRIPT.chmod(0o755)

ACTIVATE_SCRIPT
```

Test that Spack works through the activation script:

```{python}
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        """
        set -euo pipefail
        source /work/env/activate.sh
        spack find
        """,
        image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
        bind_project=PROJECT_DIR,
    ),
    tail=120,
)
```

Now inspect the activated environment:

```{python}
show_spython(
    spython_exec(
        """
        set -euo pipefail
        source /work/env/activate.sh

        echo "PATH=${PATH}"
        echo "PKG_CONFIG_PATH=${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:-}"
        echo "CPATH=${CPATH:-}"
        echo "LIBRARY_PATH=${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
        echo "LD_LIBRARY_PATH=${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
        echo "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-}"
        echo "R_HOME=${R_HOME:-}"

        which python || true
        which python3 || true
        which R || true
        spack debug report
        spack concretize --force
        """,
        image=str(TMP_SANDBOX),
        bind_project=PROJECT_DIR,
    ),
    tail=160,
)
```

If desired, write a `.envrc` for interactive developer convenience. This
should remain a wrapper around the canonical activation script, not the
canonical source of truth.

```{python}
ENABLE_DIRENV = True

if ENABLE_DIRENV:
    envrc = PROJECT_DIR / ".envrc"
    envrc.write_text(f"""
    if [ -n "${SINGULARITY_CONTAINER:-}" ] || [ -n "${APPTAINER_CONTAINER:-}" ]; then
        source /work/env/activate.sh
    fi

    LAUNCHSCRIPT="{PROJECT_DIR}/slurm/launch/launch_container.sbatch"
    """)
    envrc
```

The variables mean:

```text
PATH              finds project-provided executables
PKG_CONFIG_PATH   finds .pc files like libuv.pc
CPATH             finds headers like zlib.h and png.h
LIBRARY_PATH      finds libraries during linking
LD_LIBRARY_PATH   finds shared libraries at runtime
R_HOME            points embedded R frontends at the active R installation
```

The canonical runtime contract is:

```bash
source /work/env/activate.sh
```

`direnv` may source the same script for interactive convenience, but
Slurm jobs, VS Code tunnels, Quarto, and install scripts should source
`env/activate.sh` directly.
